title: Coral and the Echo
premise: Jonah Underhill smuggles memories between the quarantined worlds of Meridian and Halcyon, whose fleets have been frozen in a cold war since a massacre both sides remember differently. When a dead ship's manifest lists a passenger named Coral — a consciousness that shouldn't exist, stitched from stolen memories of the massacre itself — Jonah realizes she is living proof that the war's founding atrocity was manufactured. Hunting them are both fleets' intelligence services, each desperate to own or erase her. To survive, Jonah must keep alive the lie that keeps the fleets apart long enough for Coral to broadcast the truth — and choose whether a truth worth killing for is worth dying for. In the end, he lets the lie die and the truth jump through the closing window, shattering the stalemate but sparing both fleets from mutual annihilation.
about_author: August Okafor is a former marine radio operator turned novelist who writes about distance — between ships, between people, between what happened and what we agree happened. He lives in Lagos and writes at night, when the shipping lanes are quiet.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Running contraband memories past orbital customs on the Meridian–Halcyon corridor, Jonah reflects on two worlds that no longer speak and the fragile economy of forgetting that keeps him fed. A customs officer nearly catches him with a black-market memory shard. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establish the stakes of silence between worlds.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A broker offers Jonah an absurd job: verify the cargo manifest of the Calypso's Echo, a vessel destroyed in the massacre nine years ago. On its manifest, impossible and fresh: a passenger listed as 'Coral.' The job pays too well, which means someone wants it done badly. Beat: unease; the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Coral
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, shifting mid-chapter to Coral. Following the manifest trail to a derelict drydock, Jonah finds Coral: a synthesized consciousness assembled from recovered memory fragments of the massacre — including fragments both governments swore were destroyed. She remembers being everyone who died. Beat: wonder curdling into dread; first contact with the impossible.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral experiences her composite memories as overlapping lives, unable to say which grief is hers. Meridian intelligence tracks Jonah's ship; she feels their scan like hands inside her mind. Jonah decides not to sell her. Beat: identity as burden; the beginning of trust between smuggler and ghost.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Halcyon agents board under diplomatic pretense and offer Jonah his life and a fortune to hand Coral over — revealing they already know what she is. He refuses, burning a decade of careful neutrality. His oldest contact sells him out anyway. Beat: the price of survival becomes literal; betrayal.

chapters.title: What Both Fleets Remember
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Hiding in a debris field, Coral shows Jonah her memories directly: the massacre was staged by a joint command cabal to justify the quarantine that enriches both regimes. Jonah recognizes his own sister's death among the fabricated records. Beat: revelation and personal devastation; the lie has been holding everything up, including him.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The only unmonitored relay to the neutral colonies closes in seventy-two hours. Both fleets converge on the debris field, each believing the other has seized Coral as a weapon. Jonah plans a run through the blockade while Coral wrestles with broadcasting truth that could ignite open war instead of ending it. Beat: rising tension; moral vertigo before the climax.

chapters.title: Fleet Against Fleet
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jonah/Coral. The run begins; Meridian and Halcyon warships, misreading each other's pursuit of Jonah's freighter, power weapons in the corridor. Coral realizes she can broadcast through the relay from inside the crossfire — but the transmission will paint her location for every gun. Beat: climax ignition; sacrifice offered.

chapters.title: The Truth at Full Burn
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Under fire, Coral transmits the massacre's true record fleet-wide and across the relay, letting herself be targeted to hold the channel open. Jonah flies straight through the barrage to pull her core out of the wrecked transmitter bay. Beat: climax; the lie dies publicly, and survival is chosen over martyrdom.

chapters.title: Coral and the Echo
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, coda in Coral's voice. The truth spreads; both fleets stand down, their commands disgraced, the quarantine dissolving into uncertain, difficult peace. Jonah and Coral take the long route one last time — not smuggling memories now, but carrying them home. Beat: resolution; identity rebuilt, survival redefined as something shared rather than bought.
